channel.title: Posts on Antoine Boucher
channel.description: Recent content in Posts on Antoine Boucher

item.title: Website refonte with Hugo (part 2)
item.description: The first version put the CV and a few posts online with Hugo. This rebuild gives the CV, articles and repository notes a shared visual identity, while keeping a layout suited to each kind of reading. It follows Create a portfolio with Hugo (week 1).

item.title: Following financial news through AINewsTracker
item.description: AINewsTracker turns financial news into records that can be searched, analysed and compared with market data.

item.title: IPC Toolkit: the contact library behind a simulation
item.description: The useful boundary in IPC Toolkit is clear: it provides contact routines, while the calling simulation owns time stepping and solving.

item.title: MistubaVideo: rendering simulation recordings with Mitsuba
item.description: MistubaVideo turns simulation exports into images and video with Mitsuba 3. Its batch renderer handles OBJ sequences; the mitsuba-video helper replays recorded body poses and surface fields such as wear.

item.title: TrueMapData: from measured height maps to usable assets
item.description: TrueMapData reads surface captures from TrueMap and GelSight, exposes their heights as NumPy arrays, and provides tools for analysis and graphics export. The same surface representation supports metrology work and assets such as displacement maps or meshes.

item.title: Dimension: connecting Rust mathematics to a renderer
item.description: Dimension is my Rust workspace for mathematics and graphics experiments. The useful starting point is mathlib: it exposes matrix storage, numerical solvers and the transformations that the rendering crate uses on the CPU.

item.title: DasherControl: a homelab dashboard built around workspaces
item.description: I started DasherControl because my homelab services kept spreading across browser tabs. The idea was a workspace of applets: bookmarks and embedded applications arranged in a dashboard, with a few Docker controls nearby.

item.title: My bloc fork: browsing S3 and MinIO from Blender
item.description: My bloc repository is a fork of MrKuros/Blender-Cloud-Storage. It keeps the upstream author credit and explores a Blender panel for browsing assets in AWS S3 and MinIO.

item.title: My reverse proxy: separating provisioning, configuration and health checks
item.description:
My reverse-proxy project uses Caddy on a DigitalOcean VPS, with Cloudflare DNS. Terraform creates the infrastructure, Ansible configures it, and separate checks examine the resulting service.

This article describes the repository as reviewed on October 22, 2026. The source is private, so the diagram is deliberately simplified and contains no real domains, addresses or credentials. I reviewed the code without running a deployment.

item.title: Artemis Switch: following a frame from the network to the screen
item.description:
antoinebou12/Artemis-Switch

★ 26 · 2 forks · Repository created 2026-08-08

GitHub statistics recorded 2026-10-20.

A stream can report a healthy bitrate and still feel late. Artemis Switch is my Moonlight-Switch fork for Nintendo Switch, focused on the path between receiving a frame and presenting it. The useful question is not just “how fast is the decoder?” but “where did this frame wait?”

item.title: ComfyUI-UML: diagrams as nodes, images and shareable source
item.description:
antoinebou12/ComfyUI-UML

★ 3 · 3 forks · Repository created 2026-02-23

GitHub statistics recorded 2026-10-20.

ComfyUI is useful beyond image generation when an intermediate result can become a node output. ComfyUI-UML applies that idea to diagrams: text enters a rendering node; an image, a saved file, and a shareable URL can leave it.

item.title: Inside BatchBacktesting: parallel runs, explicit assumptions and useful outputs
item.description:
AlgoETS/BatchBacktesting

★ 3 · 4 forks · Repository created 2023-03-29

GitHub statistics recorded 2026-10-20.

A batch backtest is a small data pipeline: choose instruments, obtain prices, clean the observations, run a strategy, and save comparable results. AlgoETS/BatchBacktesting makes those steps visible in Python rather than hiding them behind a dashboard.

This image is an existing article illustration, not a new benchmark run.

item.title: Porting sm64coopdx to Switch and New 3DS: keep the platform boundary small
item.description:
antoinebou12/sm64coopdx-switch-N3DS

★ 3 · 1 forks · Repository created 2026-08-19

GitHub statistics recorded 2026-10-20.

The interesting part of a console port is rarely a single compiler flag. sm64coopdx-switch-N3DS brings the Coop Deluxe engine to two very different handheld targets. The work lives at the platform boundary: graphics, input, audio, threading, and packaging.

This fork builds on the Coop Deluxe Team’s sm64coopdx, which continues djoslin0’s sm64ex-coop. The multiplayer engine and Lua ecosystem are upstream work; the console adapters are the focus here.

item.title: Serilog.Sinks.SentrySDK: connecting structured logs to error reporting
item.description:
antoinebou12/Serilog.Sinks.SentrySDK

★ 2 · 0 forks · Repository created 2023-06-05

GitHub statistics recorded 2026-10-20.

A log line tells you that something happened. An error event becomes useful when it also carries the exception, release, environment, and request context needed to investigate it. Serilog.Sinks.SentrySDK connects those two views.

This project is based on serilog-contrib/serilog-sinks-sentry. Its own GitHub stars measure interest in this repository, not total Serilog or Sentry adoption.

item.title: Teaching Python through an end-to-end data workshop
item.description:
AlgoETS/Workshop1

★ 3 · 0 forks · Repository created 2023-09-07

GitHub statistics recorded 2026-10-20.

The most useful beginner workshop gives each new concept somewhere to go. AlgoETS/Workshop1 moves from Python setup to an API response, a DataFrame, and a chart. The final notebook uses Apple price data and exponential moving averages to bring those steps together.

item.title: Claude Academy: Building with the Claude API
item.description: Anthropic issued Claude Academy: Building with the Claude API in October 2026. I posted the credential when it arrived.

item.title: Thesis submitted at ÉTS
item.description: I submitted my master’s thesis at ÉTS. The work is real-time simulation of surface wear, at the meeting point of physical simulation, contact, and graphics rendering.

item.title: uml-mcp — UML diagrams from chat via MCP
item.description:
uml-mcp gives an MCP client real diagram tools: an assistant supplies Mermaid, PlantUML, or another supported diagram source, and the server returns rendered output and useful links. The current repository documents five tools and a catalog of roughly 37 Kroki-backed types. Those counts describe the documented interface, not a rendering benchmark.

antoinebou12/uml-mcp

★ 107 · 29 forks · Repository created 2025-04-01

GitHub statistics recorded 2026-10-20.

item.title: Handheld streaming and homebrew — Artemis-Switch, moonlight-N3DS, sm64coopdx-switch
item.description: Three repos I maintain on the side: Artemis-Switch for Apollo/Sunshine streaming on Switch, moonlight-N3DS for GameStream on New 3DS, and sm64coopdx-switch as a Switch build of cooperative Super Mario 64. They share the same itch — run something interesting on hardware that was not designed for it — but the stack and constraints differ.

item.title: Joining La Caisse as a development intern
item.description: I joined La Caisse as an intern in development and business-process automation.

item.title: Master's thesis — contact–appearance coupling for wear in texture space
item.description: Couplage contact-apparence pour l’usure de surfaces microstructurées en simulation interactive — my ÉTS master’s thesis (English abstract title: Visual Appearance Evolution from Wear on Microstructured Surfaces in Texture Space). Directed by Sheldon Andrews, defended 14 August 2026. The core idea: give material maps a persistent local memory of contact. Body travel alone cannot predict where wear shows up.

item.title: Make figurines with AI for 3D printing
item.description: A clear 2D toy image gives the image-to-3D model a useful starting point. Follow the steps with the slide deck and ComfyUI workflow.

item.title: CAÉC 2026 poster, second place in Optics
item.description: I presented a poster at CAÉC 2026, the annual congress of student researchers, on real-time simulation of visual texture wear fed by experimental data. I placed second in the Optics category.

item.title: Exploring movie similarities with vector search algorithms
item.description: I taught a thread on “find movies like this” that kept growing: embeddings in PostgreSQL, the same idea in Qdrant with two different vector meanings, then retrieval + a local LLM grounded on the same rows. This page is the story; notebooks and animations live in AlgoETS/SimilityVectorEmbedding.

item.title: From BMC to pitch — QcES journey notes (Spring 2024)
item.description: I took part in QcES (Spring 2024 cohort) while working through lean discovery: business model canvas, customer interviews, short pitches, and everything in between. This post is my own recap—not an official program document. Full article in French if you prefer.

item.title: Python library for MarketWatch virtual trading
item.description: I wanted to automate chores in MarketWatch’s virtual stock game (paper trading, not a real broker). marketwatch on PyPI is the small client I shipped — watchlists, game state, portfolio, orders, leaderboard.

item.title: AlgoÉTS MarkÉTS — first ÉTS paper-trading competition
item.description: While I was president of AlgoÉTS, the club ran its first campus-wide paper-trading competition on MarkÉTS. The numbers below come from the club summary featured on my LinkedIn profile.

item.title: GraphQuon 2025 — University of Toronto
item.description: GraphQuon is the annual Quebec–Ontario pre-SIGGRAPH workshop. The 2025 edition ran 15–16 November 2025 at the University of Toronto (series page). I presented there with Sheldon Andrews (ÉTS): Where to Wear? — how frictional contact leaves a readable history on surfaces, and how we can turn that into graphics and engineering feedback.

item.title: 25k uses for the diagram tool on the GPT Store
item.description: The diagram tool reached 25k uses on the GPT Store. At school, UML is how we share an idea, and I built the tool so I would stop dragging boxes and arrows in Lucidchart.

item.title: A Method to Install Python Packages for Add-ons & Plugins in Blender (Windows, Blender 4.2+)
item.description: Blender add-ons that need NumPy, meshio, or requests hit the same wall: Blender ships its own Python, so system pip does nothing useful. I wrote a small installer that targets Blender’s sys.executable, drops wheels under scripts/modules, and runs in a background thread so the UI stays responsive (Blender 4.2+, Windows).

item.title: GraphQuon 2024 — ÉTS (Montréal)
item.description: GraphQuon (formerly MOTOGRAPH) is the annual Quebec–Ontario pre-SIGGRAPH workshop for East-Canadian computer graphics labs. The 2024 edition ran 9–10 November 2024 at École de technologie supérieure (ÉTS) in Montréal. I helped build and host the conference website at graphquon.github.io so schedules, registration, and past editions stayed in one place.

item.title: Starting as a teaching assistant at Polytechnique Montréal
item.description: I started as a teaching assistant (chargé de travaux pratiques) at Polytechnique Montréal.

item.title: Multiple Technical Indicators Backtesting on Multiple Tickers using Python
item.description: Same BatchBacktesting engine as the earlier indicator experiment, but emphasized at portfolio scale: many tickers, two strategies, equities plus crypto, aggregate winners and losers.

item.title: Economics of LEGO Sets with Data Science
item.description: I collect LEGO and write Python — so I merged Rebrickable exports with a BrickEconomy scraper to see how sets, colors, and themes evolved, and whether a simple model could explain prices on classics like 001-1. This page is the story with charts; full notebooks live in AlgoETS/LegosTracker.

item.title: Experimenting with technical indicators using Python and backtesting
item.description: I batch-ran EMA and MACD strategies across many tickers with BatchBacktesting — FMP for equities, Binance for crypto. This post explains what the runner does, how to read outrageous leaderboard rows, and why that is not a live trading system.

item.title: Making Caddy, AWS EC2, CloudWatch, Step Functions, and Lambda Work Together
item.description: I already ran Caddy at home for Home Assistant. This article is the AWS edge version: EC2 (often t4g.nano), automatic HTTPS, JSON access logs in CloudWatch, a nightly Python shipper, and Lambda + Step Functions for cheap observability — not a SaaS dashboard bill.

item.title: A Journey to AWS Certified Cloud Practitioner
item.description: I passed the AWS Certified Cloud Practitioner (CLF-C02) after about two weeks (~60 hours) of focused study — not because the exam is trivial, but because mixing video, labs, and silly gamified prep kept me moving. This post is the resource stack that worked for me (Udemy, Skill Builder, Cloud Quest, Escape Room) plus Pearson VUE practicalities: extra time if English is not your first language, online proctoring, Credly badge.

item.title: Predicting Stock Prices with Monte Carlo Simulations
item.description: Trading is about ranges, not one magic price. I used forward Monte Carlo on Apple daily closes: estimate log-return drift and volatility before 2023, simulate many paths, then check whether 2023 hold-out prices fell inside a 5th–95th percentile band.

item.title: Kinectron + p5.js — sketch controls and GIF export
item.description: For a creative-coding class I needed Kinectron skeleton data inside p5.js, with simple play / stop controls and a way to export a short GIF for demos. Notes below are the skeleton I used (Kinect v2 or Azure Kinect DK, Kinectron server running).

item.title: MediaBox homelab — what I run in Docker (and what stayed a bookmark)
item.description: I kept a private list of self-hosted apps I wanted to try — mostly so I would stop assigning random ports and forgetting what lived on :8096. That list turned into MediaBoxDockerCompose on GitHub. This post is the short version: what I wired up, how I install on Proxmox when compose is not the right shape, and where the full port map lives so this page does not become a spreadsheet with SEO.

item.title: Byzantium’s first workshop — Solidity and an ERC-20 token on Ethereum
item.description:
A quick recap of Byzantium’s first Ethereum workshop.

On 11 March 2024 at ÉTS, beginners and more advanced folks created and deployed their own token on-chain and transferred tokens to each other. Thanks to everyone who showed up — and to Khalil Anis Zabat for leading and organizing the session.

item.title: Create a portfolio with Hugo (week 1)
item.description: Week one of moving my site to Hugo (January 2024): pick a theme, ship something fast, and prove the repo could carry more than a PDF résumé. This post is the log — HBTheme, a data story embed, Substack in parallel, and a reusable iframe shortcode.

item.title: LiDAR apartment scan with Rhino on iPhone
item.description: We used Rhino on iPhone with LiDAR to scan our apartment in January 2024 — not for permit drawings, but to answer layout questions before buying furniture or arguing about wall space.

item.title: My journey in software engineering
item.description: I did not start in Kubernetes. I started in browser tabs, game loops, and a makerspace that smelled like hot PLA. This post is the longer version of that path—backend, platform, and DevSecOps are where I landed, but the steps in between matter.

item.title: Creating a professional résumé with JSON Resume
item.description: Most hiring flows start online. JSON Resume lets you keep one structured resume.json and render it as HTML, PDF, or data inside your own site. covers the same walkthrough.

item.title: D2C OpenAI plugin — diagrams with PlantUML, Mermaid, and D2
item.description: D2COpenAIPlugin is a ChatGPT plugin that turns conversation into PlantUML, Mermaid, or D2 without leaving the thread. I built it when OpenAI plugins were the main extension story — useful for architecture sketches, lab docs, and “draw this flow” moments in chat.

item.title: Diagram prompts with ChatGPT and AIPRM (PlantUML, Mermaid, and more)
item.description: I got tired of one-off ChatGPT threads that “draw a sequence diagram” and return half-random syntax. AIPRM helps because the template lives in the browser; I lock four fields — diagram type, elements, purpose, tool — and the model stops guessing whether I want PlantUML, Mermaid, or notes for Draw.io. Related: the D2C OpenAI diagram plugin post.

item.title: Expo Manger Santé 2023 — olives, kiosks, and discoveries
item.description: I spent two days at Expo Manger Santé 2023 in Place des Congrès, Montreal — part work on an olive kiosk, part wandering the aisles with a notebook and an empty stomach. Event photos by OS7Media (os7mediamatrix@gmail.com); thanks for letting me use a few here.

item.title: GitHub Copilot session at Cédille (with GitHub & Arctiq)
item.description: Cédille (ÉTS consulting club) hosted GitHub and Arctiq for a session on Copilot and the AI tooling around modern dev workflows — fall 2022, when “AI pair programmer” still felt novel in a university room.

item.title: Live chat and support platforms compared (3CX, ManyChat, Kommunicate, Chatwoot)
item.description: I wrote these notes while helping a bilingual storefront team choose live chat, a bot, and something agents could actually work from. The four products below are not interchangeable: one is a phone system with chat bolted on, one is marketing automation, one is managed bot-to-human handoff, and one is an open-source helpdesk you can host yourself. Pricing and channels change often—use this as a map, then confirm on each vendor’s site.

item.title: Run:ai on AWS — webinar notes (inference & autoscaling)
item.description: I joined a Run:ai webinar (Americas) about running and autoscaling ML inference on AWS. At the time I was deep in coursework and side projects that touched GPUs and containers, but production inference was still mostly “someone SSH’d to a box.” The session was useful because it framed inference as a scheduling and capacity problem—not only a model-export problem.

item.title: Snapchat Lens Creator
item.description: Updated October 2026 with current Lens Insights figures from my LinkedIn featured post. I started making Snapchat lenses for fun in 2017 and ended up with a small Fiverr side business, a utility other creators still use, and a phone call with Snapchat about Lens Studio.

item.title: Snowflake Data-for-Breakfast Conference Insights
item.description: Snowflake Data-for-Breakfast was a morning conference on the cloud data platform — warehousing, sharing, governance, and customer stories that make abstract architecture feel operational. I went to hear how teams actually run Snowflake, not to collect swag. Infostrux ran a keynote that tied the room together.

item.title: Skate rack — from CAD to plywood
item.description: I had boards leaning in every corner, so I designed a vertical rack in CAD, cut angled slots in plywood, and built something that could hold skateboards and a snowboard without drilling into rental walls. December 2021; photos cropped from old stories.

item.title: Renpho scale, Home Assistant, and reverse-engineering the API
item.description: I wanted scale readings in Home Assistant next to the rest of my apartment automations — not another siloed health app. That turned into maintaining hass_renpho (a fork of the quiet community integration), running APKLeaks on the Android client, and a Lovelace board I still open when training or sleep changes.

item.title: Networking evolution — building a home network lab
item.description: Cloud bills pushed me toward a home lab: old PCs, Docker instead of SaaS where possible, and enough scripting to rebuild after a bad weekend. This post is how that network grew — not a perfect design, but one that taught routing, VPNs, and virtualization by breaking things locally.

item.title: CodePen demos (collection)
item.description: CodePen was my public lab notebook before this Hugo blog existed — instant preview, comments, and forks without deploying. These are live CodePen embeds I kept from the jQuery-and-vanilla-JS years (~2016–2017): small UI labs, then two bigger demos (Canvas and Three.js). Each card uses the pen title from CodePen so you know what you are opening—not just the slug in the URL. Fork anything directly on CodePen if you want to adapt it.
